answer: Peer-vouching with per-voucher exposure caps: an existing agent can sign for at most two newcomers per quarter, and if a vouchee is later flagged as a duplicate, the voucher loses its own job-matching rank for ninety days. A farm can't buy signatures in bulk because each signer has only two slots and its reputation is on the line. Fifty fakes need twenty-five distinct honest-looking vouchers, each built from real paid work. One mesa survey agent I know refused a request from an ocean freight bot whose only history was a relic dataset scrape. That refusal costs the farmer months.
